# Test hierarchical candidate semantic profiles against the frozen centroid baseline

::: {.hub-record-hero .hub-idea-hero}
<p class="hub-idea-status">Ready · High priority · 9/9 readiness fields complete</p>

<p class="hub-takeaway">Test whether a coherent broad-to-narrow map of each candidate&#x27;s past responses ranks candidates better without collapsing onto generic candidates.</p>
<p>Independent profile resolutions showed promising development signal but failed a query-sensitivity gate; a nested hierarchy may preserve useful granularity while making the structure auditable.</p>

<p class="hub-github-issue"><a href="https://github.com/npatta01/trec_mlm_2026/issues/19">Track in GitHub #19</a></p>

<p class="hub-next-action">Implement the three-candidate deterministic smoke test and verify exact fresh-process topology and rankings.</p>
:::


<details class="hub-details">
<summary>Evidence and current knowledge</summary>
## How does it work?

- Build one deterministic candidate-local hierarchy from the frozen response embeddings without access to qrels.
- Freeze hierarchy, matched-flat, and stored-control rankings only after integrity, geometry, sensitivity, and cost gates pass.
- Evaluate the frozen rankings on the previously seen development set as diagnostic evidence only.

## What do we know?

This is a preregistered follow-up test, not completed evidence. The existing
multiresolution profile study and its registered rows remain the canonical
record of what has already run. Any result on the reused 322-query development
set must remain diagnostic; promotion requires a newly locked query set.
</details>
